transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Windsor Johnston.
U.S. Central Command says it's forming a task force to help stop weapons and other restricted
materials from crossing Iran's land borders and the Caspian Sea.
CENTCOM says the effort will build on the U.S. naval blockade of Iran.
The blockade has prevented Tehran from exporting more than $25 billion in crude oil in recent
months.
Democratic control of the U.S. Senate will give the party new power over President Trump's
efforts to shape the federal courts.
NPR's Nina Totenberg says Democrats face a choice about how to use that power.
With Democrats holding at least 54 votes starting January 3rd, they will run judicial appointments
likely until 2030.
And among other things, they'll have to decide whether to slow-walk Trump's judicial nominees
or maybe even block most of them, which Republicans did in the Obama and Biden administrations,
or try to make deals on nominations with the president.
NPR's Nina Totenberg reporting.
The city of Houston will see a reduction in immigration enforcement after Democratic victories
in the Texas midterms this week.
Sarah Grunow from Houston Public Media reports.
Houston Mayor John Whitmire is directing Houston Police Department officers to reduce their
contact with immigration and customs enforcement.
That means officers in Houston will no longer be allowed to detain people solely based on
civil immigration warrants.
I do this to begin a healing process, reduce fear and anxiety across our community.
Also do this knowing that elections matter.
It's a stark difference from previous policy on police interacting with ICE, which has
drawn scrutiny and protests over the past year.
Previously, state officials blocked Houston from limiting its cooperation with ICE, threatening
to withhold millions in public safety funding.
I'm Sarah Grunow in Houston.
A promising new drug to lower the risk of heart attacks and strokes failed in its first
big test, NPR's Rob Stein reports.
Officers tested an experimental drug that can cut levels of a cholesterol-carrying particle
in the blood known as lipoprotein A or Lp(a).
The protein has long been associated with an increased risk for heart attacks and strokes.
But in a study involving more than 8,000 heart disease patients, the drug, called pellacarsin,
failed to reduce the risk for cardiovascular complications.
And failure stunned heart specialists, who had hoped drugs like this would provide the
next big advance in preventing heart disease.
But many experts say the approach may still work using other drugs or treating patients
perhaps either longer or sooner.
Rob Stein, NPR News.
It's NPR.
Protests are underway in cities across France.
Two days after a nationwide strike attracted more than a half million people.
Rebecca Rossman reports the demonstration started more than a month ago as a student
movement but has evolved into a national push for better living conditions.
France's interior minister says 70,000 police officers will be mobilized for today's protests.
What started as a student movement calling for better conditions in schools has evolved
into a national push to address wider inequalities across French society.
Today's protests come just two days after a nationwide strike drew in more than half
a million people.
Including an impromptu orchestra that assembled at the Place de la République in Paris.
Just last month, demonstrations in the same neighborhood turned violent when dozens of
businesses were looted, costing millions in damages.
The prime minister is scheduled to meet with union heads and businesses on Monday to come
up with solutions.
Rebecca Rossman, NPR News, Paris.
Your opinion officials say another round of bomb threats has targeted flights following
a series of hoaxes that forced planes to divert this week.
An airport spokesperson says nine flights to or from Prague were affected Friday.
Officials in France reported four threats against aircraft.
The defense minister in Hungary says fighter jets escorted three passenger planes through
the country's airspace.
Three broadcasters also received security threats.
No suspicious items have been found.
This is NPR.

topics.text: U.S. Central Command forms task force to block weapons flows across Iran's borders and Caspian Sea
Democrats' Senate control gives them new leverage over Trump's federal judicial nominations
Houston Mayor John Whitmire limits police cooperation with ICE, ending detentions on civil immigration warrants
Experimental heart drug pelacarsen fails to reduce cardiovascular risk in study of 8,000 patients
Protests spread across French cities as student movement becomes national push for better living conditions
Bomb threats against flights prompt diversions, affecting nine Prague flights and aircraft in France and Hungary
